hints: Use the Wilson score interval, not the normal approximation: it stays inside 0 and 1 and handles 0 and all passes.
With p = passed / n and z = 1.959964, the centre is (p + z*z/(2n)) / (1 + z*z/n), and the half-width is z * sqrt(p(1-p)/n + z*z/(4n*n)) / (1 + z*z/n).
Two results differ when their intervals do not overlap: one ends before the other starts. Overlap means this data cannot tell them apart yet. The gap between the two point estimates is not enough.
solution:
import math

Z = 1.959964


def wilson(passed, n):
    """The 95% Wilson score interval for passed out of n, as (lo, hi) fractions. n is positive."""
    p = passed / n
    z2 = Z * Z
    denom = 1 + z2 / n
    centre = (p + z2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = Z * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z2 / (4 * n * n)) / denom
    return (max(0.0, centre - half), min(1.0, centre + half))


def differ(a, b):
    """True when the Wilson intervals show a difference: they do not overlap. a and b are (passed, n).

    False means this data cannot tell the two apart yet, which does not prove they are equal.
    """
    lo_a, hi_a = wilson(*a)
    lo_b, hi_b = wilson(*b)
    return hi_a < lo_b or hi_b < lo_a
title: A 95% Wilson interval, and whether two results really differ
